name: agent-desktop
description: Computer use CLI for AI agents
one_liner: Lets an AI agent actually click buttons and type into any desktop program on your computer, the way a human would, without needing screenshots.
buyer: An operations manager at a small or mid-size company stuck using an old desktop program (insurance quoting software, legacy accounting tool) with no API, who currently pays staff to do repetitive data entry in it.
business_use_cases: An automation agency builds custom 'AI office workers' for insurance brokers and accounting firms that operate legacy desktop software nobody will ever add an API to.
A back-office outsourcing company replaces part of its human data-entry team with AI agents driving the same desktop apps those humans used.
A vertical SaaS reseller offers 'automate your clunky 2004-era desktop software' as a productized service for dental offices, auto shops, and other small businesses stuck on old tools.

money_ideas.idea: Productized RPA-style automation service: client provides the desktop app, you build and maintain the agent, billed monthly per workflow.
One-off custom automation builds for a single painful manual workflow (e.g. nightly report generation in legacy software).

steal_this: Find one small business still doing manual data entry into an old Windows desktop app, and this weekend build them a single automated workflow with this tool — then sell it as a $200/month 'set it and forget it' service.
